canonical_definition:
What it is. The definition treats FrontierMath as a benchmark for evaluating the complex problem-solving and reasoning abilities of large language models. The accompanying description also places it within reasoning benchmarks, alongside ARC-AGI, when discussing model performance.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers link FrontierMath to one construct, Reasoning, and no behavioral indicators. The recorded relationship is that Reasoning is measured by FrontierMath, and the definition likewise frames the benchmark as evaluating reasoning abilities and complex problem-solving.

Space of uses. In the usage in the papers, papers position FrontierMath as a reasoning benchmark used to report model results, and the description mentions it alongside ARC-AGI in that role. No other measurement instrument is linked to it through the recorded relationships.

relationships.evidence: Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have sparked increasing interest in the development of reasoning systems. Central to this goal are Large Language Models (LLMs) – models like OpenAI’s o1 (Jaech et al., 2024), o3 (OpenAI, 2024), or DeepSeek-R1 (Team, 2025) show complex problem-solving abilities, and demonstrate unprecedented results on reasoning benchmarks, e.g. FrontierMath (Glazer et al., 2024) and ARC-AGI (Chollet et al., 2024).
